editorial:
You are dropped right into a going-away party in New York City, where a group of friends is filming everything on a handheld camera. When a massive monster suddenly attacks the city, the celebration turns into a desperate fight to survive. The found-footage style makes you feel like you are running alongside them through the streets, dodging falling buildings and military fire. It is loud, chaotic, and genuinely scary in a way that big-budget monster movies rarely are. The characters feel like real people you might know, which makes their panic feel believable and keeps you invested from start to finish.

The acting is natural and raw, and the pacing never lets up once the monster appears. The creature design is impressive, and the sound design hits hard. On the downside, the shaky camera can be tough to watch if you get motion sick, and some characters are hard to tell apart in the dark. Still, if you enjoy intense survival stories, this is a must-see. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best experience.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the group reaches a helicopter evacuation, but the monster attacks and the helicopter crashes. Rob and Beth survive briefly and hide under a bridge, recording a final message. The camera is later found in Central Park. A brief audio clip at the end hints the monster may have come from the ocean. The twist is that the whole film is recovered footage, meaning none of them made it out alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found-footage horror and monster movies.
